context: For the height array ht = [3, 8, 5, 2, 7, 7, 3, 4], indexed from 0 to 7, container capacity is defined as cap[i, j] = min(ht[i], ht[j]) × (j - i).

Figure 15-9 moved inward from the taller board starting at [0, 7]. This figure starts from the same pair and moves the left pointer right from the shorter board. The starting heights are 3 and 4, and the capacity is 21.
description: The right pointer stays at j = 7 (height 4). The left pointer moves one position right from index 0 to i = 1 (height ht[1] = 8). Board 0 turns gray again. The left board, now 8, is taller than the right board, 4, so the shorter board is now at j = 7. A light blue rectangle from index 1 to index 7 shows the water reaching the top of the right board at height 4. The label below reads “Moving inward from the shorter board may increase capacity” and shows the capacity calculation.

frames.explanation: The width falls from 7 to 6, but the water height rises from 3 to 4. The diagram gives cap = min(8, 4) × (7 - 1) = 24. Moving inward from the shorter board can thus increase capacity, though it need not do so every time. The maximum over the whole array is still higher than 24. Figure 15-7 shows the optimal endpoints [1, 5], with capacity 28.
frames.title: Moving inward from the shorter board

summary: Moving inward from the shorter board may increase the height of the container and thus its capacity. Here the capacity rises from 21 to 24.
title: Moving inward from the shorter board
